title: Insurance inside super — permitted cover, Protecting Your Super and opt-in rules
product: Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Act 1993 and Regulations — insurance in super
version: Rule guide FY2026-27 v1.0 — current at 23 Nov 2026
summary: Which cover can be held inside super, when cover on an inactive super account stops, the opt-in rules for young people and low balances, how super-linking works, and the tax points that follow. Paraplanning uses it to recommend how cover is held; Onboarding uses it to catch cover that is about to stop; Claims uses it to find cover in super after a death or disability.
rules:
1 Permitted cover (SIS Regs reg 4.07D) — a super trustee may only provide insured benefits for events that match a condition of release: death, terminal medical condition, permanent incapacity and temporary incapacity. So new own-occupation TPD cover and trauma cover can't be held inside super; existing benefits for people who joined their fund before 1 Jul 2014 are preserved.
2 Terminal medical condition (reg 6.01A) — two registered medical practitioners, at least one of them a specialist in the relevant area, certify that the illness is likely to result in death within 24 months of the certification.
3 TPD inside super is any-occupation based — a disability super benefit needs two legally qualified medical practitioners to certify that the person is unlikely ever to be gainfully employed in a capacity for which they are reasonably qualified because of education, experience or training (ITAA 1997 s995-1).
4 Protecting Your Super (from 1 Jul 2019; SIS Act s68AAA) — a trustee must not provide insurance on a choice or MySuper product that has been inactive — no amount received — for 16 continuous months, unless the person has told the fund in writing that they want to keep the cover. The election carries over to a successor fund that gives equivalent rights.
Example: Priya Natarajan's Kestrel Retail Super account has received nothing since 30 Jul 2025, so its $50,000 death cover stops on 30 Nov 2026 unless she elects to keep it.
5 Opt-in rules (from 1 Apr 2020) — insurance needs the person to opt in if they are under 25 and new to the fund, or if their account balance is under $6,000. People who already had cover usually keep it if their balance later falls below $6,000.
6 Default cover — default life and TPD cover in super usually starts from age 25; TPD cover in super usually ends at 65 and life cover at 70.
7 Super-linking (industry practice) — one arrangement split between a policy owned by the super trustee and a policy owned personally: the cover allowed in super (life and any-occupation TPD) sits in the fund, and the cover that isn't allowed (own-occupation TPD, trauma) is held personally. The two are priced and linked together, claims are assessed against the any-occupation super cover first, and benefits from the personally owned part are paid to the individual.
8 Paying premiums from super — premiums come out of the super account rather than the household budget, and the account can be topped up by contributions or a rollover from another fund. Premiums paid through super aren't personally tax-deductible.
9 Who receives a super death benefit — the trustee pays it under the fund's rules and any valid nomination.
10 Tax on benefits from super — death benefits: a lump sum paid to a death-benefits dependant (a spouse or former spouse, a child under 18, a person in an interdependency relationship, or another dependant) is tax-free (ITAA 1997 s302-60, s302-195); for a non-dependant the taxable component is taxed at up to 15% (element taxed in the fund) or 30% (untaxed element) plus the 2% Medicare levy (s302-145). TPD lump sums: tax-free from age 60 (s301-10); below preservation age the taxable component is taxed at up to 20% plus the Medicare levy (s301-35), and the tax-free component of a disability benefit is increased by a formula (s307-145). Preservation age is 60 for people born from 1 Jul 1964.
11 Commission — commission on group super cover and on default cover in super is conflicted remuneration (Corporations Act s963B(2)), so Caldova never receives commission on default cover.
limits: No new own-occupation TPD or trauma cover inside super. Cover on an account that has received nothing for 16 continuous months stops unless the person has elected in writing to keep it. AI agents never tell a client to cancel or keep super cover — that is the client's decision with Amelia. Caldova doesn't advise on super investment options. A super death benefit is paid under the trustee's rules and any valid nomination, which may not match the client's will.
evidenceRequired: Latest super statements showing the cover, the balance and the date of the last amount received
Written election to keep cover on an inactive account (Protecting Your Super)
Trustee's nomination records for super death benefits
Medical certification required by the trustee or insurer for terminal medical condition or TPD claims
